problem: The phrase 'its centre of positive charge on top of its centre of negative charge' can be read as the two centres being separated vertically, which would contradict the next clause that there is no dipole moment.
fix: Say 'its centre of positive charge coincides with its centre of negative charge, so the two centres are not separated and it has no dipole moment of its own.'

problem: The battery-connected case only says 'the battery supplies the extra charge'. It does not say where the battery's energy goes, so a student cannot reconcile the battery work V·ΔQ with the rise in stored energy U₀ → ε_rU₀.
fix: Add: the battery drives charge ΔQ = (ε_r − 1)C₀V through a p.d. V, doing work (ε_r − 1)C₀V² = 2ΔU; half of this appears as extra stored energy ΔU and the other half is the mechanical work the field does in pulling the slab in.
